I proved these two Int.fract identities by hand while formalizing something else, but they feel general enough that they might already exist (or belong in Mathlib):

theorem fract_add_fract_eq (x y : ℝ) :
    Int.fract (Int.fract x + Int.fract y) = Int.fract (x + y)

theorem fract_sub_fract_eq (x y : ℝ) :
    Int.fract (Int.fract x - Int.fract y) = Int.fract (x - y)

The closest things I found in Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean are the existence forms Int.fract_add / Int.fract_sub (∃ z : ℤ, …) and the inequalities fract_add_le / fract_add_fract_le — but not these equalities directly. Are they already available under a name I’m missing? If not, they seem to generalize verbatim to any FloorRing, and I’d be glad to PR them. Thanks!

One issue with these lemmas is that they don't help with Int.fract (Int.fract x + Int.fract y - Int.fract y).

I think Int.fract (Int.fract x + y) = Int.fract (x + y) and Int.fract (x + Int.fract y) = Int.fract (x + y) might be better lemmas, which combine to give your lemma.
(those lemmas still don't fully help with the z version, but you can at least rewrite with commutativity associativity lemmas to get there)

Thanks Eric — that makes sense, and I agree the one-sided forms are the better primitives. I'll prepare a PR along those lines: the four one-sided lemmas (add and sub, left and right versions, since subtraction isn't commutative), with my two-sided ones derived as corollaries. I'll post the PR link here once it's up.

The PR is up: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/42080 — the four one-sided lemmas (fract_fract_add/fract_add_fract plus the two sub analogues, all @[simp]), with my two-sided forms as derived corollaries. Thanks again for the steer on the API shape!
